A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite appendix additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, calibration, adaptation and resource-consumption experiments using three ViT models and four vision benchmarks.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds ResNet-50 results, batch-size and adaptation-rate ablations, and measured neural-collapse statistics.

M1.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces NEO-BN, an evaluated variant that additionally updates batch-normalization parameters. The core NEO recentering procedure, NEO-Continual update rule and NEO-MSE algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The datasets and input scenarios remain ImageNet-C, CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-Rendition and ImageNet-Sketch, with clean ImageNet already used for latent-space analysis in v1. ResNet-50 and the new parameter sweeps expand experimental configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original seven-baseline ViT comparisons are retained. New Table 3 adds NEO-BN as an explicit comparison variant against vanilla NEO; its external comparators, SAR, TENT and CoTTA, were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the experimental design with ResNet-50 evaluation using 512 adaptation samples and severity-5 ImageNet-C, controlled batch-size and continual-alpha sweeps, and NC1–NC4 measurements. Table 4 specifies adaptation on 512 samples followed by evaluation on remaining samples. These are added protocols; the existing experiments retain their settings.

E4.justification: New analyses directly test several previously untested properties: batch-size independence at fixed adaptation sample count, continual adaptation's sensitivity to alpha, and empirical neural collapse across ViT sizes. The NEO versus NEO-BN comparison also tests adding batch-normalization updates. The batch-size sweep is distinct from v1's adaptation-sample-count study.

E5.justification: New Table 3 explicitly reports standard deviations for ResNet-50 results, whereas the retained accuracy tables report 95% confidence intervals. Existing seed statements remain unchanged. No increased run count or formal significance-testing procedure is documented for the additions.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and plots are retained, but Tables 3–5 add substantial new findings. ResNet-50 average accuracy is 23.68% without adaptation, 25.66% with NEO, 31.52% with NEO-BN and 32.14% with TENT. Table 4 reports batch-sweep accuracies of 56.91–57.04% and alpha-sweep results; Table 5 adds neural-collapse measurements. These are new-setting results, not changes to the original ViT scores.

T1.justification: Propositions 4.1, 4.2 and A.1, their assumptions and proofs, and the mathematical description of neural collapse are unchanged. The new neural-collapse table supplies empirical measurements rather than new definitions or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contribution statements and conclusion retain the same scientific claims. The introduction now explicitly mentions the continual variant's single hyperparameter, but that parameter was already disclosed in v1's method description and Table 1.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion interprets NEO's CNN results as useful where other evaluated methods degrade accuracy, explains higher-alpha performance through rapid low-sample adaptation, and characterizes ViT-Base as showing the strongest overall neural collapse. The existing limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: The additions document batch-size and alpha sweep values, adaptation/evaluation sample allocation, the ResNet-50 corruption setting, and the source of the neural-collapse metrics. NEO-BN receives only a brief procedural description. Existing code/data links, ViT checkpoint information, baseline learning rates and hardware/software specifications are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu and Papyan's 2024 Linguistic Collapse paper as the source of the neural-collapse metrics. The related-work discussion and NEO's positioning relative to prior TTA methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds three appendix subsections, briefly clarifies continual adaptation and equal sample weighting, corrects a heading typo, and updates the publication header and an affiliation. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–5, including paired ablation subtables, and renumbers the original appendix Tables 3–4 as Tables 6–7. Appendix material and the Raspberry Pi figure are repositioned through reflow. Existing figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: The CNN comparison and direct checks of batch independence, adaptation-rate sensitivity and neural collapse provide useful additional evidence while preserving the existing results. The net gain is limited by sparse NEO-BN implementation details, two differently scored rows labeled alpha = 0.01 in Table 4b, and Section 6's unchanged ViT-only evaluation limitation despite the new CNN experiment.
